rows.locus: D02's complement assertion: how a conforming-looking instrument could pass while an access hides
rows.claim: The AST string-constant complement fails closed and automatically covers every definition added after M3.4.

rows.reproduction: Run: uv run python -c 'import ast; s="def leak(c):\n t=\"\".join((\"reque\",\"sts\"))\n c.execute(f\"SELECT * FROM {t}\")"; v=[n.value for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(s)) if isinstance(n,ast.Constant) and isinstance(n.value,str)]; print(v, any(x.casefold()=="requests" for x in v))'; it prints False.

rows.disposition: CORRECTED, and narrowed. The attack's own example fails: Python concatenates ADJACENT string literals at parse time, so `'reque' 'sts'` reaches the AST as one 'requests' constant and the instrument catches it. The real hole is RUNTIME composition - explicit `+`, `.format`, f-string or `.join` - which no AST string census can see. D06 already names this class as a defect rather than a gate; the instrument is a TRIPWIRE, not a security boundary, and the contract must not claim it 'fails closed' against a hostile author. DEFERRED-S3 for the negative-control mutant that documents the boundary.

rows.locus: the every-condition quarantine promise has neither its seven-predicate inventory nor discriminating nonmatch fixtures

rows.attack: Delete the promoted-status predicate so a conflicting draft artifact is suspended too. A fixture containing only one promoted conflict still proves quarantine and passes, while no contract corpus row supplies draft, verified, wrong-scope, equal-output, or hash-versus-text nonmatches.
rows.reproduction: Run: jq -r '.rows[] | select(.id == "P04") | [.finding,.evidence] | @tsv' .agent/decisions/m3u4-map.json; the map enumerates seven WHERE predicates, but D18 and Section 9 do not carry that inventory or its negative cases.
rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless one predicate-at-a-time mutant is killed for partition, operation, revision, input hash, input JSON, unequal output, and promoted status, with reject proving zero quarantine work.
rows.disposition: DEFERRED-S3. 'Every condition' has no predicate inventory, so one promoted-conflict fixture proves quarantine while a deleted promoted-status predicate survives. The battery owns one-predicate-at-a-time mutants for partition, operation, revision, input hash, input JSON, unequal output and promoted status, with reject proving zero quarantine work.

rows.locus: zero mutation survivors is vacuous without a complete committed catalogue and mutant-liveness controls
rows.claim: A zero-survivor mutation sweep over every added or edited predicate mechanically closes the kernel-tier contract.
rows.attack: Catalogue one easy predicate, prove it killed, and omit statement order, SQL ownership, payload keys, dataclass flags, and every other predicate under a narrower interpretation of edited. The sweep truthfully reports zero survivors and its module list while grading almost nothing.
rows.reproduction: Run: /usr/bin/rg -n 'MUTATION SWEEP|zero survivors|VERDICT MODULE LIST' .agent/decisions/m3u4-contract.md; the contract requires a result and module names but specifies no catalogue cardinality, derivation, patch-liveness proof, or committed harness.
rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless a committed catalogue enumerates each changed predicate and nonpredicate obligation, every mutant proves changed bytes and loaded code, a pristine control passes, and the harness reports total, killed, equivalent, and survivor IDs.
rows.disposition: DEFERRED-S3, and it restates a standing project lesson: a survivor count is meaningless without its catalogue and its verdict modules. The battery owns a committed catalogue enumerating every changed predicate AND non-predicate obligation, a changed-bytes and loaded-code proof per mutant, a pristine control, and a harness that prints its verdict modules on the control line.

rows.locus: the projection alternative is rejected partly on an asserted SQLite materialization that the query planner does not perform
rows.claim: ALT-PROJECTION's wrapper materializes every proposal in the partition before applying the operation predicate, creating a D22 regression.
rows.attack: Run both wrapper and baseline shapes through SQLite 3.53.1 EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN. SQLite flattens the wrapper and pushes binding_operation into requests_scope; both plans search requests by partition and operation, then proposals by partition and request_id.
rows.reproduction: Run: uv run python -c 'import sqlite3; from cement_runtime.store import SCHEMA; c=sqlite3.connect(":memory:"); c.executescript(SCHEMA); q="SELECT * FROM (SELECT p.*,r.operation AS binding_operation FROM proposals p LEFT JOIN requests r ON r.partition=p.partition AND r.id=p.request_id WHERE p.partition=?) WHERE binding_operation=? AND status=\"pending\" ORDER BY id LIMIT ?"; print(c.execute("EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN "+q,("tenant_a","echo_1",10)).fetchall())'; the plan starts with SEARCH r USING INDEX requests_scope (partition=? AND operation=?).
rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless the exact committed spike query measurably visits or materializes more rows than baseline under EXPLAIN and a large collider ledger; otherwise remove this ground from the ruling.
rows.disposition: CONFIRMED, and it falsified a committed ground. Measured with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on the shipped schema under SQLite 3.53.1, the ALT-PROJECTION wrapper and the shipped statement produce IDENTICAL plans: SEARCH r USING INDEX requests_scope (partition=? AND operation=?), SEARCH p USING sqlite_autoindex_proposals_3, USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY. SQLite flattens the subquery and pushes the operation predicate down. Section 15 WITHDRAWS the D22 materialization ground. Fork 1's ruling is unchanged because it never rested on it, and the LEFT JOIN ground is now sharper: strength reduction applies only where the outer query constrains the right table, so the singular read path keeps the LEFT JOIN and returns an orphan with NULL binding columns instead of failing closed.

rows.locus: the exact CLI payload and exit contract is unnumbered, so the required one-test-per-D battery can omit it
rows.claim: Accept, correct, and reject emit the exact four-key JSON shapes in Section 13 and all retain exit code zero.
rows.attack: Keep ReviewResult correct in the library but make the CLI omit null example_id/output keys on reject or return a nonzero code. Every numbered shape, fidelity, example, and publication obligation can still pass because the exact CLI triples live only in an unnumbered ruling.
rows.reproduction: Run: /usr/bin/rg -n 'one test per numbered obligation|Exact CLI JSON|Exit code stays 0' .agent/decisions/m3u4-contract.md; the mandatory battery domain is D01-D27, while both exact CLI requirements sit outside it.
rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless a numbered obligation and committed test assert exit 0 plus the exact sorted key set and values for accept, correct, and reject, including both explicit null-valued reject keys.
rows.disposition: RESOLVED by section 15. The exact CLI triples in section 13 are an OBLIGATION, not commentary, and the battery owns one test asserting exit 0 plus the exact sorted key set and values for all three decisions, including both explicit null-valued reject keys. An unnumbered paragraph is invisible to a one-test-per-obligation battery.

rows.locus: the fork was decided on statement cardinality, but no closure instrument requires the composed adapter to retain it
rows.claim: Each adapter selection uses one statement and the composed design matches baseline statement cardinality on every consumer path.
rows.attack: Add a validation SELECT inside _proposal_bindings before its complete projection statement. D02 still attributes both requests accesses to one permitted owner, shapes and behavior remain correct, and all four listed closure instruments can pass despite recreating ALT-BINDING's rejected redundant lookup cost.
rows.reproduction: Run: jq -r '.rows[] | select(.id=="P02" or .id=="P03" or .id=="P04" or .id=="P05") | [.id,.observation.sql_statements_total,.observation.application_statements] | @tsv' .agent/decisions/m3u4-spike-binding.json; retained evidence prices statements, but Section 10 names no cardinality result.
rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless a total-channel recorder asserts the exact application and requests-statement counts for every read and all three review decisions, with each adapter call issuing exactly one statement.

A validation SELECT added inside _proposal_bindings keeps one permitted owner, correct shapes and correct behaviour while recreating the per-consumer statement cost that ruled ALT-BINDING out. The battery owns a total-channel recorder asserting exact application and requests-statement counts per path, with each adapter call issuing exactly one statement.

rows.locus: the export census does not prevent ReviewResult from widening the request-lifecycle Outcome union
rows.claim: ReviewResult is a review-only public result, while Outcome remains the unchanged handle and request_status lifecycle union.
rows.attack: Insert ReviewResult into Outcome while also exporting it alphabetically. Export count and ordering pass, review returns the right class, and runtime handle behavior stays unchanged, but the public Outcome type now advertises a request-free review result on request-lifecycle methods.
rows.reproduction: Run: uv run python -c 'from typing import get_args; from cement_runtime.models import Outcome; print([x.__name__ for x in get_args(Outcome)])'; baseline has exactly Resolved, ReviewRequired, InProgress, FallbackFailed, Rejected, and ReconciliationRequired, an inventory absent from D14.
rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless the shape census asserts the exact unchanged Outcome members and separately asserts ReviewResult export presence, alphabetical __all__ position, and exclusion from Outcome.
rows.disposition: DEFERRED-S3. Verified by hand this session - Outcome's args are exactly Resolved, ReviewRequired, InProgress, FallbackFailed, Rejected, ReconciliationRequired, with ReviewResult absent - but no TEST asserts it, so inserting ReviewResult into the union passes every export and ordering pin. The battery owns the exact unchanged Outcome member assertion beside the export census.

rows.locus: the corpus exercises the two already-clean proposal creation routes but omits handle, the sole event-payload leak
rows.claim: Every proposal event payload carries no request identity after M3.4, including legacy proposal creation through handle.
rows.attack: Run only Section 9's submit_proposal and propose creation probes; both already emit empty proposal.created payloads at baseline. The one failing route is handle, whose payload contains request_id, and the stated corpus never creates a proposal through it.
rows.reproduction: Run: /usr/bin/rg -n -C 3 'kind="proposal.created"|payload=\{"request_id"' src/cement_runtime/system.py; lines 644-650 show the direct empty payload and lines 1026-1032 show handle's request_id leak.
rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless a handle call reaching ReviewRequired asserts its proposal.created payload is exactly empty while subject_id and proposals.status_sequence remain bound to that event; retain submit_proposal and propose as controls.
rows.disposition: CORRECTED in its remedy, right about the gap, and the same defect the sibling verdict table reported as X15 from the other side. The corpus exercises only the two already-clean creation routes. The handle route IS the one leak, at system.py:1262. But its payload must NOT become empty: section 14 rules it RETAINED under the handle-lifecycle exception, because handle is not an owned site, M3.5b removes its grammar and M3.6a deletes the method. The battery asserts that payload UNCHANGED, pinning the exception.

rows.locus: the durable binding contract retains wave chronology, dispatch failure, worktree state, and origin narrative instead of dense current rules
rows.claim: The contract is an agent-optimized durable artifact containing concise binding rules, facts, warnings, and only decision-relevant grounds.

rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless the binding file retains only current obligations, concise grounds, and executable checks; move chronology and worktree provenance to an archive or evidence record and remove stale control-state prose.

Sections 12 and 13 retain wave chronology, dispatch history and worktree state, which competes with the binding obligations. Section 15 records the disposition: the narrative moves to .agent/archive/ at milestone close and the obligations stay. Not done now because the grounds are still load-bearing for S3's battery.

rows.locus: single-snapshot and transaction ownership from map X04 never became a numbered obligation or all-path probe
rows.claim: Every adapter call consumes the public method's supplied connection, opens no nested transaction, and preserves one snapshot or write lock across lookup and use.
rows.attack: Inspect connection.in_transaction, then ignore that connection and open a second read for _proposal_bindings. The stated review probe observes True on the supplied write connection and static behavior stays correct, yet lookup and companion write now span different snapshots; read paths are not probed at all.
rows.reproduction: Run: jq -r '.rows[] | select(.id == "X04") | [.finding,.evidence] | @tsv' .agent/decisions/m3u4-map.json; X04 requires one supplied connection in all five methods, while Section 9 observes in_transaction only inside review.
rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless all five public paths assert one transaction call, adapter connection identity, and no nested connect/transaction; a review race must prove lookup and status write share the same write transaction.
rows.disposition: DEFERRED-S3. Observing connection.in_transaction on the supplied connection does not prove the adapter USED it, so a second read opened inside the adapter passes the stated probe while lookup and companion write span different snapshots. The battery owns connection IDENTITY assertions across all five public paths plus a review race proving lookup and status write share one write transaction.

rows.locus: malformed JSON is a real STRICT-ledger ValueError path, contradicting D24's fabricated-only exception premise
rows.claim: A raw TypeError, ValueError, or OverflowError cannot arise from a real ledger on these paths; any such probe is fabricated.
rows.attack: Create a supported pending proposal, update its TEXT input_json to malformed JSON without changing schema, and call get_proposal. parse_json raises public ValidationError, which subclasses ValueError, directly from a real STRICT ledger; no row proxy or schema rewrite is involved.
rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless real-ledger malformed JSON on get_proposal, proposal, proposals, review, and function_report is translated to IntegrityError; reserve fabricated labels for proxy-only storage classes.
rows.disposition: RESOLVED by section 15, and it disproves D24's premise with a real-ledger path. A supported pending proposal whose TEXT input_json is rewritten to malformed JSON is a schema-valid STRICT row, and parse_json raises ValidationError, a ValueError subclass, with no proxy and no schema violation. D24 must translate real-ledger malformed JSON to IntegrityError on all five paths.

rows.locus: the scope promises that no ledger consumer loses information while the ruled public payload deliberately removes and redefines values
rows.claim: Nothing is deleted from the schema and no consumer of the ledger loses information in M3.4.
rows.attack: Compare the operator payloads: accept/correct consumers lose request_id, source, and artifact_id and receive a changed status value; proposal readers also lose request_id. Storage retains the bytes, but public ledger consumers plainly lose access to information.
rows.reproduction: Run: jq -r '.rows[] | select(.id == "P08") | .observation.baseline_accept_json' .agent/decisions/m3u4-spike-binding.json; it prints six public keys, while Section 13's accept payload has four and changes status.
rows.acceptance_check: Fail unless Section 1 narrows the claim to no stored schema or row information is deleted and explicitly lists the intentional public information losses and status transformation.
rows.disposition: RESOLVED by section 15, and the claim was false as written. Public consumers do lose access: accept and correct lose request_id, source and artifact_id, proposal readers lose request_id, and status changes value. Section 1 now claims only that NO STORED SCHEMA OR ROW INFORMATION IS DELETED, with the public losses enumerated as intentional.
